title: Add a reproducible archival and restoration integration harness
body:
<!-- liquivault-backlog:archival-recovery -->

## Candidate progress

The reusable contracts runner and sibling SDK example have three recorded successful instrumented-localhost receipts, including the 13 November 2026 rerun. They demonstrate natural instance/position expiry, exact automatic-restoration keys, rejected signing without restoration, confirmed withdrawal and exact balance changes. See docs-local-integration.md and the shared docs/gates receipts. Canonical contract timing and public testnet records are unchanged. The original separate restore/confirm/rebuild criterion below remains open: the exercised Protocol 28 path restores atomically with the withdrawal. Manual fallback and production-timing coverage are not claimed. This is a local draft until explicitly refreshed on GitHub.

## Original context

TTL helpers exist, but simulation does not renew rent and no automated restoration integration test is shipped.

title: Expose an explicit restoration planning API
body:
<!-- liquivault-backlog:archival-planning -->

## Post-rejection candidate progress

Partially implemented: planContractCall reports normal, automatic-restoration and manual-restoration-required modes with network/source/sequence, fees and keys. Tests preserve Protocol 23 restore-list data. Automatic archived-network integration now passes on an instrumented localhost fixture, including rejected signing and confirmed withdrawal. A caller-authorized manual recovery executor and its failure coverage remain unfinished; do not close this issue as complete. This progress note is a local draft until explicitly refreshed on GitHub. Original acceptance criteria follow for review.

## Original context

Current protocols can automatically restore archived entries using simulation-provided restore lists. The SDK relies on official preparation for that path, but has no caller-visible planner for restoration costs or a tested manual fallback for oversized/operator-sponsored recovery.

## Scope

`src/wallet/rpc.ts`

## Suggested complexity

High; final Wave complexity is set by maintainers in the Drips app.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Expose restoration requirements, affected entries and cost information without signing, submitting or spending by surprise.
- [ ] Test the normal Protocol 23+ automatic restore-list path. Provide explicit caller-authorized manual restoration only when needed, confirm it and rebuild the original call afterwards.
- [ ] Test restoration-needed, rejected restoration, failed restoration and successful recovery.
- [x] Keep footprint/auth data tied to the selected network and document sequence/fee behavior.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck && npm test && an opt-in restoration integration command`
